newsitem.title: UK: UK-Belgium gas pipeline awards onshore contracts.
newsitem.headline: UK-Belgium gas pipeline awards onshore contracts.

text.p: The UK-Belgium natural gas pipeline consortium Interconnector on Thursday awarded contracts worth about 160 million stg (US$250 million) for onshore work associated with the subsea link, Interconnector said in a statement.
The pipeline, due to open in 1998, will transport gas from Bacton on Britain's east coast to Zeebrugge in Belgium.
The contracts for the design and construction of onshore facilities at Bacton and Zeebrugge were awarded to Kvaerner unit Kvaerner John Brown.
Four gas turbine/compressor packages will be supplied by the Thermodyn unit of French state-owned nuclear concern Framatome, with the turbines sub-contracted to GE's Nuovo Pignone.
Inconnector managing director Roger Cornish said preparatory work had already started on the project, worth a total of about 487 million pounds ($770 million).

Interconnector partners are British Gas (10 percent, British Petroleum (10 percent), DuPont's Conoco (10 percent), Elf Aquitaine, Gazprom (10 percent), Distrigaz (5 percent), Ruhrgas (5 percent), Amerada Hess (5 percent) and National Power (5 percent).
